questions.question: What do the stone-carved wheels of the Konark Sun Temple symbolically depict?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Measurement of time cycles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **stone-carved wheels** of the **Konark Sun Temple** are iconic structures that symbolically depict the **measurement of time cycles**. These wheels are not merely decorative but have a significant astronomical and functional value.
 
• Each of the wheels represents a **sun dial**, functioning as a tool to measure time. The intricate carvings and divisions on the wheels align with the hours, minutes, and seconds of the day. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The design of the wheels reflects the ancient Indian understanding of **astronomy** and the passage of time through celestial movements. These wheels are integral to the temple's association with the **Sun God, Surya**, who symbolizes the cyclic nature of time. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The wheels consist of **24 spokes**, symbolizing the 24 hours of a day. The divisions further denote smaller units of time, emphasizing the advanced knowledge of timekeeping possessed by the architects of the temple.
 
• The positioning and orientation of the wheels are aligned with the **movement of the sun**, showcasing the synchronization between architecture and astronomy. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• While the wheels primarily depict the measurement of time cycles, they also signify the cyclic nature of life and time, a recurring theme in Indian philosophy.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Measurement of time cycles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Konark Sun Temple:**

 
 
• The **Konark Sun Temple**, located in **Odisha, India**, was built in the **13th century** by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
 
• The temple is dedicated to the **Sun God, Surya**, and is designed in the shape of a colossal chariot with **12 pairs of intricately carved wheels** and seven horses.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Wheels:**
 
 
• The wheels are not just artistic elements but serve as **functional sundials**. By observing the shadow cast by the central axle of the wheels, one can determine the time of the day.
 
• The **24 spokes** represent the hours of a day, and the carvings on the wheels illustrate the **cyclic nature of time** in Indian cosmology.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Brilliance:**
 
 
• The positioning of the wheels aligns with the **movement of the sun**, reflecting the advanced astronomical knowledge of the builders.
 
• The temple itself is a masterpiece of **Kalinga architecture**, showcasing intricate carvings, sculptures, and engineering marvels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**

 
 
• The **Konark Sun Temple** was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1984** due to its cultural and architectural significance.
 
• It is considered one of the finest examples of **Indian temple architecture** and is a major tourist attraction.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Challenges:**
 
 
• The temple has suffered damage over the centuries due to **natural calamities**, invasions, and lack of maintenance.
 
• Efforts are being made by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** to restore and preserve this historical monument.

questions.question: What is the name of the festival observed alongside Karam by unmarried tribal girls in Jharkhand and nearby regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawa** is a significant cultural and religious festival observed by **unmarried tribal girls** in the state of **Jharkhand** and its neighboring regions.
 
• This festival is celebrated in conjunction with the **Karam festival**, which is one of the most important festivals of the tribal communities in the region, particularly among the **Oraon, Munda, and Santhal tribes**.
 
• The primary focus of the **Jawa festival** is to pray for prosperity, fertility, and better agricultural productivity. It also emphasizes the health and well-being of the family. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• During this festival, the young tribal girls plant **Jawa seeds (barley or paddy)** in a small basket filled with fertile soil. These seeds are then nurtured with care and devotion over a period of **seven to nine days**.
 
• On the day of the festival, the **Jawa plants** are used as offerings during the main ritual performed by the community. The festival is marked by traditional songs, dances, and rituals. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• The synchronized celebration of **Karam** and **Jawa** highlights the deep connection of tribal communities with nature and their agricultural way of life.
 
• The festival also provides an opportunity for young girls to bond, celebrate their culture, and pray for a prosperous future. Hence, the statement is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karam Festival:**

 
 
• The **Karam festival** is one of the most prominent tribal festivals in **Jharkhand** and is dedicated to the worship of the **Karam tree**, which symbolizes fertility, prosperity, and the well-being of the community.
 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm by the **Oraon, Munda, and Santhal tribes**. The festival involves traditional rituals, songs, and dances, focusing on the importance of nature in the lives of the tribal people.
 
• The festival is celebrated during the **monsoon season** when the Karam tree is worshipped, and the community seeks blessings for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Jawa Festival:**
 
 
• The **Jawa festival** is celebrated alongside the Karam festival by unmarried girls, who plant and nurture **Jawa seeds** (barley or paddy) as a symbolic act of devotion and hope for prosperity.
 
• It provides an opportunity for young girls to showcase their dedication, celebrate their cultural heritage, and pray for a bright future.
 
• The synchronized celebration of Karam and Jawa signifies the deep-rooted connection of tribal communities with **agriculture and nature**.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Festivals:**
 
 
• **Sohrai:** This is a harvest festival celebrated by the tribes of Jharkhand to mark the season of reaping crops and is accompanied by rituals and traditional art forms like **Sohrai paintings**.
 
• **Sarhul:** This is a spring festival celebrated by tribal communities to worship trees and nature for their role in sustaining life. It marks the beginning of the **new year** as per the tribal calendar.
 
• **Madai:** This is a festival celebrated by the tribal communities of **Chhattisgarh**, involving traditional rituals, dance, and music to honor their deities and seek blessings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Tribal Festivals:**

 
 
• Tribal festivals like **Karam** and **Jawa** hold immense cultural and religious importance as they signify the deep connection of tribal communities with **nature and agriculture**.
 
• These festivals also serve as occasions for social bonding, community participation, and the preservation of tribal traditions and heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of Unmarried Girls in Jawa:**
 
 
• The participation of unmarried girls in the Jawa festival emphasizes their role in nurturing and sustaining life, both symbolically and culturally.
 
• The rituals performed during Jawa not only highlight the importance of agriculture but also reinforce the values of **care, dedication, and hope** for a prosperous future.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the essence of traditional music from Rajasthan?

options.text: Rooted in nature, daily life, and folklore

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rooted in nature, daily life, and folklore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Traditional Rajasthani music** is deeply connected to **nature, daily life, and folklore.** It reflects the cultural richness and heritage of the region.
 
• The music is often inspired by **natural surroundings, desert landscapes**, and the daily lives of the people, including their joys, struggles, and festivities.
 
• **Folklore and storytelling** play a significant role in Rajasthani music, where songs narrate tales of **historical heroes, deities, and love stories.** Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The instruments used in traditional Rajasthani music, such as the **sarangi, dholak, algoza, and kamaycha**, are indigenous and crafted locally. This highlights its **rooted nature in traditional practices.**
 
• **Statement 1:** Restricted to worship practices only - This is incorrect because Rajasthani music is multifaceted and includes genres like devotional music, folk songs, and celebratory music.
 
• **Statement 2:** Dominated by modern electronic instruments - This is incorrect as traditional Rajasthani music primarily uses **acoustic and traditional instruments**, although fusion with modern techniques is seen in contemporary renditions.
 
• **Statement 4:** Limited to elite classical traditions - This is incorrect because Rajasthani music is **accessible to all**, and its folk nature bridges all social and economic classes.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Rooted in nature, daily life, and folklore.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Traditional Music of Rajasthan:**

 
 
• Rajasthani music includes various forms such as **bhajans, panihari songs, maand, and ballads.**
 
• Devotional songs like **bhajans** are dedicated to deities like Krishna and Shiva, showcasing its spiritual aspect.
 
 
 
• **Key Instruments:**
 
 
• Traditional instruments like **sarangi, kamaycha, morchang, and algoza** are integral to Rajasthani music.
 
• These instruments are handcrafted and often made using **local materials**, reflecting the region's culture.
 
 
 
• **Folk Themes:**
 
 
• Themes of Rajasthani music often revolve around **love, valor, festivals**, and the **challenges of desert life.**
 
• **Examples:** Songs narrating the tales of **Pabuji and Dhola-Maru** are popular in Rajasthani folklore.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Variations:**

 
 
• Different regions of Rajasthan have unique musical styles, such as **Maand** from Jodhpur and **Panihari** songs from Marwar.
 
• Each style is influenced by **local traditions, dialects, and instruments.**
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Artists and organizations are working to **preserve Rajasthani folk music** by promoting performances and recordings globally.
 
• Festivals like the **Rajasthan International Folk Festival (RIFF)** celebrate and highlight the region's musical traditions.
 
 
 
• **Global Influence:**
 
 
• Rajasthani music has gained international recognition, influencing **fusion music projects** and collaborations with artists worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is prohibited under handball rules?

options.text: Using hands to intercept a flying ball
Striking the ball from an opponent’s grasp
Stopping the ball with the upper body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Striking the ball from an opponent’s grasp**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Striking the ball from an opponent’s grasp** is prohibited in handball. According to the rules of the game, players are not allowed to forcibly snatch or strike the ball out of an opponent's hands. Such actions are considered a foul and may lead to penalties. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Using hands to intercept a flying ball** is a legal action in handball. Players are allowed to use their hands to block, catch, or intercept the ball in motion. This is a fundamental skill in handball and does not violate the rules. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Bouncing the ball before passing** is also permitted in handball. Players can dribble or bounce the ball as part of their gameplay, similar to basketball. It is a common and essential technique used to navigate the court. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Stopping the ball with the upper body** is also allowed in handball. Players can use their hands, arms, and even their upper torso to stop or control the ball. This action is completely within the rules. *This statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Handball Overview:**

 
 
• **Handball** is a fast-paced team sport played between two teams of seven players each. The objective is to score goals by throwing the ball into the opponent's net.
 
• The game is governed by the **International Handball Federation (IHF)**, which sets the rules and regulations for professional and amateur matches worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Rules Regarding Ball Possession:**
 
 
• Players are allowed to hold the ball for a maximum of **3 seconds** and take up to **3 steps** while holding the ball before passing, shooting, or dribbling.
 
• Defensive players are not permitted to strike the ball out of an opponent's hands as this disrupts fair play.
 
 
 
• **Actions Allowed in Handball:**
 
 
• Players can use their hands to block, pass, and shoot the ball, provided they follow the rules of possession.
 
• Using the upper body to control or stop the ball is a common and legal action in handball.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fouls in Handball:**

 
 
• Fouls include actions like pulling, hitting, or pushing an opponent, as well as striking the ball out of their hands.
 
• Serious fouls may lead to penalties, such as a 7-meter throw for the opposing team or temporary suspension of the player at fault.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Handball:**
 
 
• The game is played on a court measuring **40 meters by 20 meters**, with goals at each end.
 
• Each match consists of two halves, each lasting **30 minutes**, with a halftime break of **10 minutes**.

questions.question: What was the primary responsibility of the Board of Control formed under Pitt’s India Act?

options.text: Regulation of civil and military governance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulation of civil and military governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pitt’s India Act of 1784** was enacted to address the shortcomings of the **Regulating Act of 1773**, particularly the governance and administration of the East India Company in India.
 
• This act brought the **East India Company’s administration in India under British government control**. It aimed to introduce a dual system of governance to regulate both commercial and political affairs.
 
• The formation of the **Board of Control** under this act was a significant step. Its primary responsibility was the **regulation of civil and military governance** in British India. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• The Board of Control was composed of six members, including the **Chancellor of the Exchequer** and a Secretary of State. The board was vested with supervisory powers over the administration and governance of British India.
 
• The act also maintained the Company’s commercial privileges but ensured that political decisions were subject to the control of the British government. *This dual control system marked a significant shift.*
 
• The Board of Control had powers to direct the **Governor-General and Council** in India regarding civil, military, and revenue matters, ensuring alignment with British interests.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Regulation of civil and military governance.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pitt’s India Act of 1784:**

 
 
• The act was introduced by **William Pitt the Younger**, the then Prime Minister of Britain, to reorganize and regulate the administration of the East India Company.
 
• The act established a dual system of control where the **commercial activities** of the company were managed by the Court of Directors, while the **political affairs** were under the Board of Control.
 
 
 
• **Board of Control:**
 
 
• The Board of Control was responsible for overseeing and regulating the civil, military, and revenue administration in India.
 
• It had the authority to inspect and approve all correspondence between the East India Company and its officials in India.
 
• **Key members** of the board included prominent British officials like the Chancellor of the Exchequer and a Secretary of State.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Pitt’s India Act:**
 
 
• The act ensured better regulation of the East India Company’s activities and brought India’s administration under closer scrutiny of the British Parliament.
 
• It marked the beginning of a systematic approach to governance, laying the foundation for future administrative reforms in India.
 
• It also paved the way for greater British intervention in Indian affairs, eventually leading to the end of the company’s rule in 1858.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Pitt’s India Act:**

 
 
• The act distinguished between the **commercial** and **political functions** of the East India Company.
 
• It allowed the British government to exercise direct control over the company’s political activities while maintaining its commercial autonomy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Act:**
 
 
• This act marked the beginning of British governmental control over Indian administration, which continued to expand over time.
 
• It highlighted the growing realization of the importance of India as a colony and the need for more effective governance mechanisms.

questions.question: Who secured India’s first Olympic medals at the 1900 Paris Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Norman Pritchard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Norman Pritchard** was the first Indian athlete to win an Olympic medal at the **1900 Paris Olympics**.
 
• He won **two silver medals** in the **200 meters sprint** and the **200 meters hurdles** events.
 
• Pritchard's achievements marked a significant milestone in Indian sports history as he was the first Indian-born athlete to compete and win at the Olympics.
 
• He competed under the banner of **British India**, as India was under British rule at the time.
 
• Despite controversies surrounding whether he represented India or Britain, the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** officially recognizes him as an Indian athlete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Norman Pritchard's Background:**

 
 
• Born in **Calcutta (now Kolkata)** in **1875**, Pritchard was a British citizen residing in India.
 
• He was an accomplished athlete and was also known for his contributions to football and cricket in India.
 
 
 
• **Events at 1900 Paris Olympics:**
 
 
• The **200 meters sprint** was one of the most competitive events, where Pritchard secured a silver medal behind **Walter Tewksbury** of the USA.
 
• In the **200 meters hurdles**, Pritchard earned his second silver medal, demonstrating his prowess in track and field events.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Norman Pritchard's success paved the way for future Indian athletes and inspired participation in global sports events.
 
• He later moved to the USA, where he became a successful actor in Hollywood, using the stage name **Norman Trevor**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Milkha Singh:**

 
 
• Milkha Singh, also known as the "Flying Sikh," represented India in the **1960 Rome Olympics** but did not win any medals.
 
• He was a celebrated Indian sprinter who narrowly missed a bronze medal in the 400 meters event.
 
 
 
• **K. D. Jadhav:**
 
 
• Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic medal (bronze) in **wrestling** at the **1952 Helsinki Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand:**
 
 
• Dhyan Chand, known as the "**Wizard of Hockey**," led India to **three Olympic gold medals** in **1928, 1932, and 1936**.
 
• However, field hockey was a team event, and he did not win any individual medals.

questions.question: Match the Taekwon-Do terms with their meanings and choose the correct combination:1. Tae2. Kwon3. Do4. DojangWhich of the following pairs is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Taekwon-Do** is a Korean martial art that combines combat techniques, self-defense, sport, exercise, and philosophy.
 
• The term "Taekwon-Do" is derived from three Korean words: **Tae**, **Kwon**, and **Do**.
 
• **Tae:** Refers to "foot strike" or kicking techniques. It represents the use of the feet for attack and defense. Hence, statement 1 (Tae-Foot strike) is *correct*.
 
• **Kwon:** Refers to "hand strike" or punching techniques. It denotes the use of hands or fists in combat. Hence, statement 2 (Kwon-Hand strike) is *correct*.
 
• **Do:** Refers to "the way" or "path," symbolizing the philosophical aspect of Taekwon-Do that focuses on self-improvement and discipline. Hence, statement 3 (Do-Way) is *correct*.
 
• **Dojang:** Refers to the "training hall" where Taekwon-Do practitioners train and practice their skills. Hence, statement 4 (Dojang-Training hall) is *correct*.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of Taekwon-Do:**

 
 
• Taekwon-Do originated in **Korea** in the mid-20th century and is now practiced worldwide. It emphasizes both physical and mental development.
 
• The martial art is characterized by its **dynamic kicking techniques, speed, and agility**. It is popular as a sport, and its philosophy focuses on **discipline, respect, and self-control**.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Terms:**
 
 
• **Tae:** Represents the use of feet for techniques like kicks, blocks, and strikes. Kicking is a defining characteristic of Taekwon-Do.
 
• **Kwon:** Symbolizes the use of hands or fists in punching, blocking, and striking techniques. Hand techniques are essential for close-range combat.
 
• **Do:** Reflects the philosophical foundation of Taekwon-Do, emphasizing personal growth and the journey toward mastering one's mind and body.
 
• **Dojang:** Serves as the training area where practitioners learn and refine their skills. It is considered a sacred space for martial arts training.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Taekwon-Do became an official Olympic sport in **2000**, highlighting its global popularity.
 
• It is governed internationally by organizations such as the **World Taekwondo Federation (WTF)** and the **International Taekwon-Do Federation (ITF)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Training and Philosophy:**

 
 
• Taekwon-Do training involves physical drills, sparring, and forms (patterns), which are sequences of movements used to simulate combat scenarios.
 
• The philosophy of Taekwon-Do encourages practitioners to embody values like **integrity, perseverance, self-control, and respect**.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• It is used for self-defense, fitness, competitive sports, and personal development.
 
• Taekwon-Do competitions include sparring matches, breaking techniques, and forms demonstrations.
 
• It is practiced by people of all ages, making it a versatile martial art suitable for children, adults, and seniors alike.

questions.question: The Trilateral Highway Project seeks to connect India with which two Southeast Asian nations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar and Thailand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Trilateral Highway Project** aims to connect **India, Myanmar, and Thailand** via a well-developed road network. It is a significant initiative under India's "Act East Policy."
 
• The project involves the construction and upgradation of a highway connecting **Moreh (India), Tamu (Myanmar), and Mae Sot (Thailand)**. This will enhance connectivity between Southeast Asia and India.
 
• The highway spans approximately **1,360 kilometers** and is designed to promote trade, economic integration, and cultural exchanges among the three countries.
 
• India is playing a major role in the project by funding and executing several stretches of the highway in **Myanmar**, as well as conducting feasibility studies and providing technical expertise.
 
• The project is expected to facilitate seamless movement of goods and people, reducing transit times and transportation costs in the region.
 
• **Myanmar** serves as a crucial link between India and Thailand, making it an essential partner in the highway project. It provides the geographical continuity required for the connection.
 
• The highway is also part of broader regional connectivity initiatives like the **Asian Highway Network** and the **ASEAN-India Connectivity Project**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Myanmar and Thailand.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India’s Act East Policy:**

 
 
• The **Act East Policy** was introduced by India in **2014** to deepen ties with Southeast Asian and East Asian countries. It replaced the earlier "Look East Policy."
 
• It focuses on strengthening economic, strategic, and cultural relations with countries in the **ASEAN region** and beyond.
 
• The Trilateral Highway Project is a key component of this policy, as it aims to improve connectivity and foster regional integration.
 
 
 
• **Myanmar’s Role:**
 
 
• **Myanmar** acts as a geographical and logistical bridge between India and Thailand. Its inclusion in the project is vital for the success of the highway.
 
• India is assisting Myanmar in building and upgrading key road stretches, such as the **Kalewa-Yagyi section**, to improve infrastructure in the region.
 
 
 
• **Thailand’s Role:**
 
 
• **Thailand** is one of the main beneficiaries of the project as it enhances trade routes and tourism opportunities between Thailand, Myanmar, and India.
 
• Thailand is actively collaborating on the project to ensure smooth operational connectivity between Mae Sot and other regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Benefits of the Trilateral Highway Project:**

 
 
• It will enhance **trade and commerce** between India, Myanmar, and Thailand, boosting economic growth in the region.
 
• It promotes **people-to-people contact**, cultural exchange, and tourism opportunities among the three countries.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• The project faces challenges such as **political instability** in Myanmar, funding issues, and delays in construction timelines.
 
• Addressing infrastructure gaps and ensuring security along the highway are also critical concerns.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The Trilateral Highway Project has the potential to expand further to include other **ASEAN countries**, integrating the region more comprehensively.
 
• It aligns with India's vision of a more connected and prosperous **Indo-Pacific region**.

questions.question: What is the central theme discussed in the book Why Bharat Matters?

questions.question: Identify the correct order of blood flow through the chambers of the human heart.

options.text: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Left atrium → Left ventricle
Left atrium → Left ventricle → Right atrium → Right ventricle
Right ventricle → Left atrium → Right atrium → Left ventricle
Left ventricle → Right ventricle → Left atrium → Right atrium

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right atrium → Right ventricle → Left atrium → Left ventricle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blood flow through the heart follows a specific pathway, ensuring oxygenation and circulation throughout the body.
 
• **Step 1: Right Atrium:** Blood enters the heart through the right atrium, which receives **deoxygenated blood** from the body via the **superior vena cava** and **inferior vena cava**.
 
• **Step 2: Right Ventricle:** The blood flows from the right atrium to the right ventricle through the **tricuspid valve**. The right ventricle pumps the deoxygenated blood to the lungs via the **pulmonary artery**. This step is crucial for blood oxygenation. *Hence, this step is correct.*
 
• **Step 3: Left Atrium:** Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs to the left atrium through the **pulmonary veins**. This marks the transition of blood from the pulmonary circulation to systemic circulation.
 
• **Step 4: Left Ventricle:** Blood flows from the left atrium to the left ventricle through the **bicuspid/mitral valve**. The left ventricle, the strongest chamber of the heart, pumps oxygenated blood to the entire body through the **aorta**. *Hence, this sequence is correct.*
 
• The sequence ensures the blood is oxygenated in the lungs and circulated effectively to meet the body's needs.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Right atrium → Right ventricle → Left atrium → Left ventricle.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Circulatory Process:**

 
 
• The human heart is a **four-chambered organ** responsible for pumping blood throughout the body. It consists of **two atria** (right and left) and **two ventricles** (right and left).
 
• The **right side** of the heart handles **deoxygenated blood**, sending it to the lungs for oxygenation via the **pulmonary circulation**.
 
• The **left side** of the heart pumps **oxygenated blood** to the body through the **systemic circulation**.
 
 
 
• **Heart Valves:**
 
 
• **Tricuspid Valve:** Located between the right atrium and right ventricle, it prevents backflow of blood into the atrium.
 
• **Mitral Valve:** Located between the left atrium and left ventricle, it ensures one-directional blood flow.
 
• **Pulmonary Valve:** Prevents backflow of blood from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle.
 
• **Aortic Valve:** Prevents backflow of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle.
 
 
 
• **Role of Pulmonary Circulation:**
 
 
• Pulmonary circulation involves the movement of blood from the heart to the lungs and back, ensuring oxygenation of blood.
 
• Deoxygenated blood is sent to the lungs via the pulmonary artery, while oxygenated blood returns through pulmonary veins.
 
 
 
• **Systemic Circulation:**
 
 
• Systemic circulation distributes oxygenated blood to the body and returns deoxygenated blood to the heart.
 
• The aorta is the primary artery responsible for systemic blood flow.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Heart as a Double Pump:**

 
 
• The human heart functions as a double pump, with the right side managing pulmonary circulation and the left side handling systemic circulation.
 
• This dual-pump mechanism ensures that oxygen-depleted blood is sent to the lungs and oxygen-rich blood is sent to the body.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Valves:**
 
 
• Heart valves play a critical role in maintaining unidirectional blood flow and preventing backflow during the cardiac cycle.
 
• Valve malfunctions, such as stenosis or regurgitation, can lead to heart conditions that affect blood circulation.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Importance:**
 
 
• Understanding the pathway of blood flow is crucial for diagnosing and treating cardiac conditions such as heart failure, valvular disorders, and congenital defects.
 
• Medical imaging techniques like echocardiography are used to visualize and assess heart function.

questions.question: What happens when a sound wave travels from air into water?

options.text: Frequency remains constant while wavelength changes
Wavelength stays constant but frequency rises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency remains constant while wavelength changes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound Wave Characteristics:** When a sound wave moves from one medium (e.g., air) to another (e.g., water), its **speed and wavelength change**, but the **frequency remains constant**. This occurs because the frequency is determined by the source of the sound and does not depend on the medium.
 
• **Frequency:** The frequency of the sound wave remains constant during the transition because it is governed by the vibrating source. *Hence, the statement that frequency remains constant is correct.*
 
• **Wavelength:** The wavelength changes because it is influenced by the speed of sound in the new medium. Water has a higher density and elasticity than air, leading to a faster speed of sound and a longer wavelength in water. *Hence, the statement about wavelength change is correct.*
 
• **Speed of Sound:** The speed of sound increases as it enters water from air due to water’s greater density and elasticity compared to air. This change in speed directly impacts the wavelength, as wavelength is proportional to the speed of sound. *Hence, the statement about the speed increase is correct.*
 
• ***In summary:** When a sound wave travels from air to water, the **frequency remains constant** while the **wavelength increases** due to the higher speed of sound in water.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**

 
 
• The speed of sound varies in different media due to their **density** and **elasticity**. It is approximately **343 m/s** in air, **1482 m/s** in water, and much faster in solids like steel (**5960 m/s**).
 
• The higher speed in water is due to its greater density and ability to transmit compressional waves more efficiently compared to air.
 
 
 
• **Relationship Between Speed, Frequency, and Wavelength:**
 
 
• The equation governing this relationship is **v = f × λ**, where:
 
 
• **v:** Speed of sound in the medium
 
• **f:** Frequency of the sound wave (constant)
 
• **λ:** Wavelength of the sound wave
 
 
 
• As the speed of sound increases in water, the wavelength increases proportionally, keeping the frequency constant.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sound Waves in Different Media:**
 
 
• **Sonar Technology:** Utilizes the high speed of sound in water for underwater navigation and object detection.
 
• **Medical Imaging:** Ultrasound uses sound waves in water-based media to produce images of internal organs.
 
• **Acoustics:** Understanding sound propagation in air and water is essential for designing musical instruments and soundproof environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Physical Properties of Media:**

 
 
• **Density:** Water's higher density compared to air makes it a better medium for transmitting sound waves.
 
• **Elasticity:** The elasticity of the medium determines how efficiently sound waves propagate. Water’s higher elasticity contributes to the faster speed of sound.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• **Underwater Communication:** Submarines use sound waves to communicate and detect objects underwater.

questions.question: The provision for a Uniform Civil Code is included under which part of the Indian Constitution?

__
 
• The provision for a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** is mentioned under **Article 44** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** in the **Indian Constitution**. It directs the State to secure a UCC for all citizens.
 
• The purpose of the UCC is to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing all citizens. This is to ensure **equality, uniformity, and secularism** in laws related to marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, and maintenance.
 
• The **Directive Principles**, including Article 44, are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a **welfare state**.
 
• The **objective** of the UCC is to ensure that all citizens of India are treated equally under the same set of secular civil laws, irrespective of their religion, gender, or caste.
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India has, in many judgments, advocated for the implementation of the UCC. For example, in the **Shah Bano case (1985)**, the Court urged the government to move toward formulating a UCC. *Hence, the correct answer is Directive Principles of State Policy.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **What are Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)?**

 
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are a set of guidelines or principles given to the central and state governments of India, listed in **Part IV** of the Constitution.
 
• They are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** and are inspired by the concept of a **welfare state**.
 
• Although not enforceable by the courts, these principles are considered **fundamental** in the governance of the country and aim to promote social and economic democracy.
 
 
 
• **Important Features of Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code):**
 
 
• **Article 44** states that "The State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India."
 
• It aims to replace personal laws based on religious scriptures and customs with a common law applicable to all citizens irrespective of religion.
 
• The **UCC** is seen as a way to achieve **gender equality**, provide equal rights to women, and promote national integration.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Observations on UCC:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** has repeatedly stressed the need for a UCC in judgments such as the **Shah Bano case (1985)**, Sarla Mudgal case (1995), and Danial Latifi case (2001).
 
• In the **Sarla Mudgal case**, the Court emphasized that the implementation of the UCC is necessary to harmonize conflicting interests and ensure social justice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why is the UCC significant?**

 
 
• The UCC is essential for ensuring **gender equality, secularism, and national integration**. It eliminates discrimination based on religion and gender in personal laws.
 
• It has been a topic of significant debate in India due to its implications for **religious freedom and cultural diversity**.
 
• It is viewed as a step toward achieving the constitutional vision of **equality and justice** for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementing UCC:**
 
 
• Religious diversity in India poses a significant challenge to the implementation of a uniform code, as personal laws are deeply rooted in religious practices.
 
• Resistance from various religious communities due to concerns over the erosion of cultural identity and religious freedom.
 
• The lack of political consensus has also hindered the progress toward implementing the UCC.

__
 
• **Assertion (A): Delhi often reports extremely high Air Quality Index values.**

 
 
• The **Air Quality Index (AQI)** is a measure used to assess the quality of air and the presence of pollutants in the atmosphere.
 
• Delhi frequently experiences poor air quality due to factors like **vehicular emissions, industrial pollution, construction activities**, and crop stubble burning in neighboring states.
 
• The city's air quality often reaches hazardous levels, especially during winter months when **smog and particulate matter** concentrations increase. *Hence, statement A is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): Its geographical position restricts air movement due to surrounding landforms.**
 
 
• Delhi's geographical location in the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** contributes to the accumulation of pollutants.
 
• The region is surrounded by the **Himalayas in the north**, which act as a barrier and prevent the dispersal of air pollutants.
 
• During winter, the cold weather and lack of strong winds exacerbate the situation, causing pollutants to stagnate in the atmosphere. *Hence, statement R is correct.*
 
 
 
• Since the geographical position of Delhi (**Reason R**) plays a significant role in contributing to the city's high AQI values (**Assertion A**), the reason provided is a correct explanation for the assertion. *Hence, the correct answer is option 1.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):**

 
 
• The **AQI** is categorized into six levels: Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, and Severe.
 
• Pollutants such as **PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, Ozone, and Ammonia** are measured to determine AQI levels.
 
• Delhi often records AQI values in the "Very Poor" or "Severe" category due to high concentrations of **PM2.5** and **PM10**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Factors Affecting Delhi's Air Quality:**
 
 
• Delhi's location in the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** limits the dispersion of pollutants due to its flat terrain.
 
• The presence of the **Himalayan range** blocks the movement of air and traps pollutants in the atmosphere.
 
• Seasonal factors such as **low temperatures, high humidity, and lack of wind** during winter months exacerbate pollution levels.
 
 
 
• **Human Activities Contributing to Pollution:**
 
 
• Burning of **crop stubble** in neighboring states like Punjab and Haryana adds significantly to Delhi's pollution.
 
• High vehicular emissions due to the dense population and increasing number of vehicles further worsen air quality.
 
• Industrial emissions, construction activities, and waste burning are major contributors to air pollution in the region.

• **Government Initiatives to Combat Pollution:**

 
 
• The **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** has been implemented to tackle pollution based on AQI levels.
 
• Efforts to curb stubble burning include providing subsidies for alternative farming practices and machinery.
 
• Promotion of cleaner fuels and electric vehicles is underway to reduce vehicular emissions.
 
 
 
• **Health Impacts of Air Pollution:**
 
 
• Exposure to high levels of pollutants like **PM2.5** can cause respiratory issues, cardiovascular diseases, and other health complications.
 
• Long-term exposure can lead to chronic illnesses and reduced life expectancy.

questions.question: Which regions of India are well known for extensive coral reef formations?

options.text: Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coral reefs** are marine ecosystems formed by the accumulation of calcium carbonate skeletons of coral organisms. They thrive in shallow, warm, and clear waters.
 
• India is home to significant coral reef formations in specific regions, particularly the **Gulf of Kutch**, **Gulf of Mannar**, **Lakshadweep**, and **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**.
 
• These regions provide the ideal conditions for coral reef growth, such as **tropical climates, warm waters, and nutrient-poor environments**.
 
• Coral reefs in India play a crucial role in **coastal protection**, supporting **marine biodiversity**, and providing **livelihoods** to local communities.
 
• **Eastern coastal river deltas**: These areas receive heavy sedimentation from rivers, which is not conducive to coral reef formation. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Western coastal plains only**: While the western coast has some coral formations, they are not as extensive or significant as those found in specific regions like the Gulf of Mannar or Andaman & Nicobar Islands. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Deep offshore ocean beds**: Coral reefs require sunlight for photosynthesis through symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae). Deep ocean beds lack sunlight, making them unsuitable for reef development. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Coral Reef Regions in India:**

 
 
• **Gulf of Kutch:** Located in Gujarat, this area has fringing reefs. It is known for its adaptability to extreme temperature variations and high salinity levels.
 
• **Gulf of Mannar:** Found between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka, it contains one of the most biodiverse reef ecosystems in India. It was declared a **Biosphere Reserve** in **1989**.
 
• **Lakshadweep:** This archipelago features atoll reefs and is known for its pristine coral formations, supporting diverse marine life.
 
• **Andaman & Nicobar Islands:** These islands have fringing and barrier reefs. The clear, warm waters of this region support vibrant coral ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Coral Reefs:**
 
 
• **Types:** Coral reefs are classified into fringing reefs, barrier reefs, and atolls based on their structure and location.
 
• **Importance:** Coral reefs act as natural barriers protecting coastlines from erosion, storms, and tsunamis. They also support marine biodiversity and provide resources for fisheries and tourism.
 
 
 
• **Threats to Coral Reefs:**
 
 
• **Climate Change:** Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching, which can lead to large-scale reef die-offs.
 
• **Pollution:** Agricultural runoff and industrial pollutants damage reef ecosystems.
 
• **Overfishing:** Unsustainable fishing practices deplete reef-associated fish populations, disrupting the ecosystem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Efforts:**

 
 
• The Indian government has designated several coral reef regions as **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)** to conserve biodiversity.
 
• **National Coral Reef Monitoring Programme (NCRMP):** This initiative monitors coral reef health and promotes sustainable management practices.
 
 
 
• **Global Importance:**
 
 
• **Coral Triangle:** While not in India, the Coral Triangle in Southeast Asia is known as the "Amazon of the Seas" due to its immense biodiversity.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution defines States and Union Territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 1** of the **Indian Constitution** defines the name and territory of India. It states that **"India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States."**
 
• It establishes the structure of India as a **"Union of States"**, ensuring the integrity and sovereignty of the nation.
 
• **States and Union Territories** are categorized under **Schedules 1 and 8** of the Constitution, with their respective names and territories mentioned here.
 
• **Article 1(2)** specifies the territories of India, which include:
 
 
• The territories of the states.
 
• The Union territories specified in the First Schedule.
 
• Any other territories that may be acquired.
 
 
 
• **Article 1(3)** affirms the inclusion of new territories into the Union of India through various means like acquisition, integration, or other legal processes.
 
• The classification of **States and Union Territories** is essential for administrative purposes and governance. *Hence, Article 1 defines this structure.*
 
• The **Union of States** is an integral feature of the Indian Constitution, emphasizing that the Indian Union is indestructible, while the states' boundaries can be reorganized under **Article 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Article 1:**

 
 
• **Article 1** plays a significant role in defining India as a union and its territories.
 
• The inclusion of territories enables India to accommodate newly acquired areas or make administrative changes when required.
 
 
 
• **Article 239:**
 
 
• **Article 239** deals with the **administration of Union Territories** by the President through an administrator appointed by him.
 
• It does not define the states or Union Territories but ensures their governance mechanism under the Union Government.
 
 
 
• **Article 240:**
 
 
• **Article 240** provides the President with the power to make regulations for certain Union Territories like **Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli**, and others.
 
• It does not define the territories but grants legislative powers for governance.
 
 
 
• **Article 32:**
 
 
• **Article 32** is known as the **"Right to Constitutional Remedies."** It allows individuals to move to the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• It does not have any direct connection to the definition of states and Union Territories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Article 1:**

 
 
• It reflects the federal structure of the Indian political system, where power is divided between the Union and the states, but the Union remains indissoluble.
 
• Article 1 is crucial for defining India's territorial integrity and maintaining its sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Schedules Related to States and Union Territories:**
 
 
• **First Schedule:** Lists all the states and Union Territories along with their territorial boundaries.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** Defines the division of powers between the Union and the States through three lists – Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.

questions.question: Consider the statements:1. Delegated legislation is framed by executive authorities under delegated powers.2. Such legislation is immune from judicial review.Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Delegated legislation** refers to the process whereby legislative powers are delegated by the legislature to the executive or another subordinate authority. The legislature enacts a parent or enabling act, and under this act, the executive frames detailed rules, regulations, or orders to operationalize the law. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• However, delegated legislation is **not immune from judicial review**. Courts have the authority to examine such legislation to ensure that it does not exceed the powers conferred by the enabling act or violate constitutional provisions. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The judiciary, through the doctrine of ultra vires, can strike down delegated legislation if it exceeds the limits of the powers granted by the legislature or if it is inconsistent with the parent act or the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delegated Legislation:**

 
 
• It is also known as subordinate or secondary legislation.
 
• It is framed by bodies like the executive (government departments, ministries, or statutory authorities) under powers delegated by the legislature.
 
• **Examples:** Rules and regulations framed by ministries under acts like the **Factories Act, 1948**, or the **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**.
 
• The parent act or enabling act specifies the framework, objectives, and boundaries within which delegated legislation must operate.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review of Delegated Legislation:**
 
 
• Courts have the power to review delegated legislation to ensure that it does not exceed the authority conferred by the parent act (ultra vires).
 
• Delegated legislation can be challenged on grounds such as:
 
 
• **Substantive Ultra Vires:** When the legislation exceeds the powers granted by the enabling act.
 
• **Procedural Ultra Vires:** When the procedural requirements laid down by the enabling act are not followed.
 
• **Violation of Fundamental Rights:** If the delegated legislation contravenes provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Examples:** In the case of **In Re Delhi Laws Act (1951)**, the court upheld the validity of delegated legislation but emphasized that it must conform to the Constitution and the enabling act.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Delegated Legislation:**
 
 
• It helps in addressing the technical and dynamic aspects of governance, which the legislature may not be equipped to handle in detail.
 
• Ensures flexibility and adaptability in the implementation of laws.
 
• Reduces legislative workload by allowing the executive to frame detailed rules and regulations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Delegated Legislation:**

 
 
• Enables technical experts to frame detailed rules.
 
• Facilitates faster law-making, especially in emergencies.
 
• Ensures flexibility in responding to changing circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Delegated Legislation:**
 
 
• May lead to excessive delegation, undermining the authority of the legislature.
 
• Risk of misuse by the executive, leading to arbitrary or unconstitutional rules.
 
• Over-reliance on delegated legislation can dilute parliamentary control.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Safeguards:**
 
 
• The judiciary ensures that delegated legislation adheres to the principles of the rule of law and remains within the ambit of the parent act.
 
• The courts act as a check against arbitrary or excessive use of delegated powers by the executive.

questions.question: What primarily causes temperature rise in the thermosphere during intense solar activity?

options.text: Absorption of ultraviolet and X-ray radiation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Absorption of ultraviolet and X-ray radiation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Reason for temperature rise in the thermosphere:** The thermosphere experiences a significant rise in temperature during intense solar activity. This is because of the **absorption of high-energy ultraviolet (UV) and X-ray radiation** emitted by the Sun.
 
• **Role of UV and X-ray radiation:** These radiations are absorbed by molecules and atoms in the thermosphere, including oxygen and nitrogen. This absorption process causes the molecules to gain energy, leading to increased temperatures. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The thermosphere is the **fourth layer of Earth's atmosphere**, located above the mesosphere and below the exosphere. This layer is highly responsive to solar activity.
 
• During periods of intense solar activity, such as solar flares or coronal mass ejections, the Sun emits greater amounts of high-energy radiation, leading to a pronounced temperature increase in the thermosphere. *Hence, intense solar activity directly impacts this process.*
 
• Other factors like molecular collisions, convection currents, and cloud formation processes are not primarily responsible for the temperature rise in the thermosphere. Their role in this context is minimal or negligible. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• **Layers of Earth's Atmosphere:**

 
 
• **Troposphere:** The lowest layer, where weather phenomena occur. It extends up to approximately 8-15 km above Earth's surface.
 
• **Stratosphere:** The layer above the troposphere, extending up to about 50 km. It contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
 
• **Mesosphere:** The third layer, extending from 50 km to about 85 km. It is where meteors burn upon entering Earth's atmosphere.
 
• **Thermosphere:** The fourth layer, extending from 85 km to about 600 km or more. It experiences high temperatures due to the absorption of solar radiation.
 
• **Exosphere:** The outermost layer, where atmospheric particles gradually escape into space.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of the Thermosphere:**
 
 
• It is characterized by low density of molecules and a significant rise in temperature with altitude.
 
• The thermosphere is home to the **ionosphere**, a region with charged particles that plays a crucial role in radio communication and auroras.
 
• **Temperature:** Temperatures can rise to 2,500°C or more, depending on solar activity.
 
 
 
• **Solar Activity and Its Effects:**
 
 
• **Solar flares and coronal mass ejections:** These events release significant amounts of energy, including UV and X-ray radiation, which directly impact the thermosphere.
 
• **Geomagnetic storms:** High-energy particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field, leading to increased ionization and heating in the thermosphere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Ultraviolet and X-ray radiation:**

 
 
• These radiations are absorbed by oxygen and nitrogen molecules, splitting them into ions and increasing kinetic energy, which manifests as heat.
 
• **Applications:** The thermosphere's properties make it suitable for placing satellites, as it provides limited drag due to its low density.
 
 
 
• **Space and satellite operations:**
 
 
• The thermosphere is a critical region for space exploration, as it houses satellites, including the International Space Station (ISS).
 
• During periods of high solar activity, increased drag can affect satellite orbits, necessitating adjustments.
